title: Partial weight download + retries — scratchpad
body:
Notes to self — high level:

Symptom: intermittent model load failures when pulling sharded checkpoint from S3. Failures happen ~1-3% of attempts (observed in dedi pool warmup) and usually resolved after retrying download or reattempting load. Goal: identify root cause(s) and create mitigations (retry logic, validation, alerting).

Observed error snippets (from loader logs / Python stack):
- EOFError / Unexpected EOF:
  RuntimeError: Unexpected EOF while reading file (expected 2147483648 bytes, got 673290)
- Torch load / state_dict mismatch:
  KeyError: 'model.layers.27.self_attn.k_proj.weight' not found in checkpoint index
- Checkpoint index complaint:
  ValueError: index.json references 8 shards but only 7 files present: missing model.weights.0007.pt
- HTTP / S3 errors during multipart:
  curl: (18) transfer closed with 123456 bytes remaining to read
  botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (InvalidPart) when calling the CompleteMultipartUpload operation: The specified upload does not exist
- Checksum/etag mismatch during local verify:
  expected sha256: 3a7f... but computed: 1d2c...

Commands & things I tried (raw):
- Basic list and size checks:
  aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models/ggml-large-v2/2025-11/ --recursive --human-readable
  du -h model_dir/* | sort -h
- Download attempts:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/large-checkpoint/model.weights.0000.pt ./ --no-progress --only-show-errors
  aria2c -x10 -s10 "https://storage.internal/redwood/ckpt/model.weights.0001.pt" --auto-file-renaming=false --continue=true
  curl -v -L --fail --retry 5 -o model.weights.0002.pt "<signed-url>"
  wget --tries=20 --timeout=30 -c "<signed-url>" -O model.weights.0003.pt
- Partial download + range tests:
  curl -r 0-1048575 -o head.bin "<signed-url>"   # first 1MB
  curl -r 1048576-2097151 -o mid.bin "<signed-url>" # next 1MB
- Checksum locally:
  sha256sum model.weights.0000.pt && md5sum model.weights.0000.pt
- Quick inspect (python):
  python - <<PY
import torch, os
fn='model.weights.0000.pt'
print(os.path.getsize(fn))
try:
    sd=torch.load(fn, map_location='cpu')
    print('loaded keys', list(sd.keys())[:10])
except Exception as e:
    print('load err', repr(e))
PY

What behaved weirdly / signals: 
- Partial downloads are present with final file size smaller than expected, but S3 reports the correct object size. This points to transfer aborts (curl/wget/aria2) or a proxy dropping connection.
- ETags: some shards have ETag values that look like multipart upload ETags (contains dashes). Our current checksum verification expects single-part sha256 stored in metadata, so multipart uploads complicate verification.
- Some shards that failed to load were actually valid if re-downloaded immediately — suggests transient network glitches or corrupted local write.
- In one case, index.json referenced a gzipped shard (model.weights.0005.pt.gz) but loader didn't gunzip automatically; caused KeyError due to file mismatch. Need to reconcile manifest semantics vs loader expectations.
- Observed race in dedup/copy pipeline: uploader process finishes S3 complete-multipart step slightly after metadata index is pushed to registry -> consumers see index before all parts fully available. Might explain occasional InvalidPart errors.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Network/transient close on client side leaving truncated files on disk -> loader sees smaller file and errors. Fix: atomic download + temp file then move + verify size & checksum.
2) Manifest/index version mismatch: newer publishers started gzipping some shards and adjusted naming; older loader code doesn't handle .gz suffix. Fix: handle gzip transparently or enforce publisher invariants.
3) Race between S3 CompleteMultipartUpload and index publish -> index claims object exists but parts not committed globally yet. Fix: uploader should block until S3 version is accessible, or index publish should be delayed until HEAD returns 200 consistently.
4) Proxy / CDN rewriter corrupting range requests (internal infra issue). Fix: escalate to infra/network, capture tcpdump for failing run.
5) Checksum verification insufficient for multipart objects (ETag not sha256). Need to persist sha256 in object metadata at upload time; if impossible, compute server-side manifest entry with sha256.

Repro steps (minimal instructions):
1) Pick model: s3://redwood-models/ggml-test/partial-repro/ (seeded reproducer bucket)
2) Run a loop of parallel downloads (10 concurrent) using aws s3 cp and curl/aria2 alternately for same shard files. Repeat ~200 times to elevate chance.
3) Occasionally you'll see truncated file sizes and loader errors described above.

Temporary mitigations shipped already (notes):
- Added local atomic write: download -> .part -> verify size -> rename to final. (PR in serve:1389)
- Loader now validates expected file size from index before attempting torch.load and raises early with clear message.
- Quick retry: if load fails and file size < expected, auto-redownload up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff.

Open follow-ups / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm uploader pipeline waits for S3 HEAD to be stable after CompleteMultipartUpload (ask infra).
- [ ] Add server-side sha256 in manifest entries for all models (engineering + model-team coordination).
- [ ] Add unit/integration test in CI that simulates truncated downloads (use stubbed http with connection close).
- [ ] Investigate gzip-handling mismatch; add loader support for .pt.gz transparently or enforce naming constraints in publisher.
- [ ] Add end-to-end alert: percent of loads that required >1 download -> page on threshold.
- [ ] Collect tcpdump for a reproducible failure window and share with network infra if pattern shows connection resets.

Random debugging notes / heuristics I want to remember: 
- If file size matches index but torch.load still fails -> probably file-level corruption (not truncation). Check sha256.
- ETag with dash usually means multipart upload; cannot trust ETag for content hash.
- aria2 with lots of splits sometimes triggers server-side throttling -> incomplete files. For large shards we prefer single-threaded download with resume (-c).
- mmap-opened shards behave differently; use map_location='cpu' to avoid weird cuda OOM during partial load.

Slack pings I sent: 
- @riley: saw InvalidPart error, can you check the uploader's CompleteMultipart logs for model ggml-test?
- @samira: pushed small PR for atomic download + early size validation (serve#1389).

If this becomes a bigger outage: rollback option is to pin to previous model version (non-sharded single-file) and reroute traffic. But need to ensure fallback model meets SLA.

End of scratchpad. Will clean up and formalize into incident postmortem if we get a reproduce.
